books.title: Lord of the Mysteries
books.content: An absolute masterclass in worldbuilding. This story and world has forever changed my relationship with fantasy, as I am forever just looking for something to match the intense emotions and connection I feel towards this world and characters. This book found me at a time where I was slipping away from literature as a whole and pulled me right back into it and for that I will be forever grateful.

books.title: Reverend Insanity
books.content: An incredible story sadly left unfinished. Yes the worldbuilding is excellent and the characters are well written, but the plot that seems to have every single thread thoroughly thought through

books.title: Born A Crime
books.content: Baby's first exploration into internalised and institutionalised racism. This book was my first look into truly what it meant to be an other and what it meant to truly live as a second class citizen, and ultimately what has allowed me to realise my own country's institutionalised racism. This book, funny and amusing as it may be opened my eyes to the discrimination and pain that so many go through and how to take a step back and look at the situations of the world.

books.title: Speaker For The Dead
books.content: A book that I can comfortably say had the intricacies and novelty fly over my head when I first read it. Definitely benefited from a second read where the implications of the story had a deeper impact.

books.title: Animal Farm
books.content: Easy introduction to the concept of greed is evil, with simple language that makes the themes feel even more unnerving. I was forced to read this short story by my english teacher, and what I can say about it now is that I will be forcing my own children to read it.

books.title: Atonement
books.content: An excellent example of an unreliable narrator, and a book that reads better on multiple reads. This novel made me grapple with my own ideas of what atonement truly meant. Just because I was sorry with all my heart did not mean that the harm I had caused was done with, nor did it mean that I deserved to be absolved of my guilt by the people around me. Given my situations were not so dire, but yet it pushed me properly reflect and internalise the ways in which I presented myself in this world.

books.title: The Handmaids Tale
books.content: A book that gets much better when looked at through an analytical lense. Many references and deeper themes were originally lost on me during a casual read were put to the forefront when I was forced to look for references or specific wordplay throughout. It put me in the position of a woman with no control in her life, and without having read this book, I would not have been able to truly appreciate the struggle of living in a theocracy nor the difficulties of being a woman.

books.title: Steel Ball Run
books.content: A beautiful and incredibly weird story. I can't say that this manga resonated with me because of its incredibly deep themes around desire and personal growth, however what really stuck with me was the sheer absurdity of it contrasted with those themes.This manga lead me to the understanding that being able to enjoy and understand intellectual concepts and notice deep literaly themes, does not mean the literature in question needs to be bleak for the sake of it, sometimes it can simply be wonderfully bizarre.
